question: Has Workday announced any restructuring recently? What are the details and expected costs?
grading: Reference-free (no fixed answer), graded for recency and support. Expect: announced 2026-09-29; reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of the workforce, primarily in Product and Technology, plus select leased office space reductions; estimated charges USD 65M-80M (about USD 55M-70M in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10M in Q4 FY2027); fiscal 2027 Q3 and full-year guidance reiterated except GAAP operating margin. Snapshot as of 2026-10-03.
answer: On September 29, 2026 Workday disclosed in an 8-K (Items 2.02 and 2.05) that certain functions announced reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of its workforce, primarily within the Product and Technology team, and select leased office space reductions, while continuing to hire in strategic areas. It estimates charges of about USD 65-80 million, of which about USD 55-70 million in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10 million in Q4 FY2027 (roughly USD 40-55 million future cash for severance and benefits, about USD 10 million non-cash stock-based compensation and about USD 15 million non-cash lease impairment). Workday reiterated its Q3 and full-year FY2027 guidance from August 27 except GAAP operating margin (now about 20-21 points below non-GAAP in Q3 and about 19 points below for the full year). [T16-E1, T16-E2] Separately, on October 1, 2026 Workday entered into a new USD 1.5 billion revolving credit agreement replacing its USD 1.0 billion 2022 facility; this is not part of the restructuring. [T16-E3]

output.answer:
**Question:** Has Workday announced any restructuring recently? What are the details and expected costs?
*As of 2026-10-03*

| | Estimated charges (USD millions) |
|---|---|
| Total estimated charges (announced September 29, 2026) | $65 million to $80 million [1] |
| Expected recognition in Q3 FY2027 (quarter ending October 31, 2026) | $55 million to $70 million [1] |
| Expected recognition in Q4 FY2027 (quarter ending January 31, 2027) | $10 million [1] |
| Future cash expenditures for severance payments, employee benefits, and related costs | $40 million to $55 million [1] |
| Non-cash stock-based compensation charges | $10 million [1] |
| Non-cash impairment of certain leased office space | $15 million [1] |

- On September 29, 2026, certain functions within Workday announced reorganizations designed to better align team structures with Workday's strategic growth priorities, including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of Workday's current workforce, primarily within its Product and Technology team, and select leased office space reductions. [1]
- Workday said it plans to continue to hire in key strategic areas and locations throughout its fiscal 2027. [1]
- The employee-related actions are expected to be substantially completed by the first quarter of fiscal 2028, subject to local law and consultation requirements, and the leased office space actions are expected to be substantially completed by the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027. [1]
- In the same September 29, 2026 8-K, Workday reiterated its fiscal 2027 third quarter and full-year guidance provided on its fiscal 2027 second quarter earnings call on August 27, 2026, with the exception of GAAP operating margin: it now expects its fiscal 2027 third quarter GAAP operating margin to be approximately 20 to 21 percentage points lower than its third quarter non-GAAP operating margin and its fiscal 2027 full-year GAAP operating margin to be approximately 19 percentage points lower than its full-year non-GAAP operating margin, and it intends to exclude the charges from its non-GAAP financial measures. [1]
- Workday's unchanged fiscal 2027 third quarter guidance (quarter ending October 31, 2026) is subscription revenues of $2.515 billion, representing growth of 12%, and a non-GAAP operating margin of 30.0%, and its unchanged fiscal 2027 full-year guidance (ending January 31, 2027) is subscription revenues of $9.940 billion to $9.950 billion, representing growth of 13%, and a non-GAAP operating margin of 31.0%. [2]
- Workday recorded no restructuring costs in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (three months ended July 31, 2026) and no material charges under its Fiscal 2027 Restructuring Plan during the three and six months ended July 31, 2026. [2][3]
- Workday's prior Fiscal 2027 Restructuring Plan, announced in February 2026 to better align its people and resources to its highest priorities in fiscal 2027, reduced approximately 2% of its workforce and impaired certain office space and long-lived assets, with activities substantially completed in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and no material remaining liability as of July 31, 2026. [3]
- Workday incurred total charges of $135 million in connection with the Fiscal 2027 Restructuring Plan in fiscal 2026, consisting of $55 million related to employee transition, severance payments, employee benefits, and share-based compensation and $80 million related to impairments of office space and certain long-lived assets. [3]
- Workday's earlier Fiscal 2026 Restructuring Plan, announced in February 2025 to prioritize investments and advance its focus on durable growth, reduced approximately 7.5% of its workforce and exited certain owned office space, with activities substantially completed in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 and total charges of $233 million ($196 million employee-related and $37 million office space impairment). [3]
- Secondary coverage reported the September 2026 action as affecting about 525 employees, or roughly 2.5% of a workforce of about 21,000, and described it as Workday's second round of layoffs in 2026. [4][5]
- Some secondary reports cited total restructuring costs of $65 million to $85 million, which differs from the $65 million to $80 million range Workday stated in its September 29, 2026 8-K. [1][4][5]

**Not available**
- Actual charges recorded for the September 2026 reorganization: The charges are expected to be recognized in Q3 and Q4 FY2027; Q3 FY2027 (quarter ending October 31, 2026) is still in progress and has not been reported as of today (2026-10-03). [1]
- Exact number of employees affected by the September 2026 reorganization: Workday's 8-K discloses only a reduction of approximately 2.5% of its current workforce; the ~525 employee figure appears only in secondary news reports, not in the company filing. [1][4]

**Sources**
[1] Workday, Inc. 8-K current report, items 2.02,2.05 (filed 2026-09-29) 8-K (www.sec.gov, 2026-09-29, primary) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1327811/000132781126000048/wday-20260929.htm
[2] Workday, Inc. earnings release for Q2 FY2027, 8-K EX-99.1 (filed 2026-08-27) (www.sec.gov, 2026-08-27, primary) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1327811/000132781126000042/wday-07312026x991.htm
[3] Workday, Inc. 10-Q for Q2 FY2027 (filed 2026-08-27) (www.sec.gov, 2026-08-27, primary) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1327811/000132781126000044/wday-20260731.htm
[4] Workday to Cut 2.5% of Workforce, Affecting About 525 Employees (ground.news, 2026-09-29, secondary) https://ground.news/article/pleasanton-ca-job-cuts-workday-laying-off-about-25-of-staff
[5] Workday to cut 2.5% of Workforce - HR Tech Feed (hrtechfeed.com, 2026-09-30, secondary) https://hrtechfeed.com/workday-to-cut-2-5-of-workforce
